policy: Conservative manually maintained ledger, supported by independent reviews that may be performed by AI agents. Add a certification only after the full named environment has source review, compiled actual exports and permitted transitive axioms. Partial components, algorithms and source obstructions do not count. All unlisted named environments remain uncounted. This is not a percentage of the entire monograph. Record fields added on 2026-11-10 (project decision 2026-11-10, site redesign spec §5): `proof_origin` (source-proof: formalizes the book's argument; source-proof-repaired: the book's argument with gaps repaired, see the cited source issue; own-proof:source-cites: the book cites the literature and the Lean proof is this project's own; own-proof:source-omits: the book gives no proof and the Lean proof is this project's own), `display_note` (how the proved statement differs from the print), `correction_status` (proposed-by-project: the correction, restriction or repair is this project's proposal, not confirmed by the authors; none is author-confirmed). `status_override` may only downgrade a record's displayed status (currently only "incomplete" on Theorem 7.7). `entry_display_notes` holds display notes for statement entries that have no record here (superseded entries, reading aids and prose-claim entries).

proved_variants.statement_scope: Restricted: the printed theorem asserts that a model-based algorithm, namely Q-FTRL, attains the rates, but the monograph omits Q-FTRL (marl.tex:432) and leaves A and Õ undefined (C39). The existential guarantee is proved from scratch with an explicit reconstructed witness: optimistic Hedge (entropic FTRL) with backward induction and per-agent adaptive generative queries. The witness is not shown to be Q-FTRL, and it is not model-based (it builds no empirical transition kernel). With one universal constant C, quantified before all sizes (the proof gives C = 20000), for every δ ∈ (0,1), ε ∈ (0,H], known reward (bounded on steps 1..H) and every transition kernel, with probability ≥ 1−δ: (i) N ≤ C·H⁴S·Σ_iA_i·ε⁻²·log(4HSΣ_iA_i/δ) adaptive, randomized generative queries give an ε-CCE (joint output, gap ≤ ε); (ii) for two-player zero-sum games (r₂ = −r₁, r₁ ∈ [0,1]), N ≤ C·H⁴S·A·ε⁻²·log(8HSA/δ) queries give an ε-NE product policy, with A read as max(A₁,A₂), which implies the A₁+A₂ and A₁ = A₂ readings. The query count is deterministic; Õ is read as a universal constant times one log(·/δ) factor with no ε in the logarithm. The algorithm sees the reward but not P. Adds the domain binders S ≥ 1 and A_i ≥ 1. The two clauses are separate existentials sharing C; that one algorithm serves both is argued in prose only. Whether Q-FTRL itself attains the rate is not checked. Not author-approved; this does not prove the printed theorem. Project decision 2026-11-10: the proved entry is an existential witness, not the printed Q-FTRL algorithm and not a special case of the printed theorem, so the printed Theorem 7.7 is shown as incomplete (status_override) with this existence result as a related proved result.
proved_variants.display_note: Not a special case of the printed Theorem 7.7. The printed theorem is about Q-FTRL, a model-based algorithm the monograph does not specify (marl.tex:432). What is proved is that some algorithm attains the printed rates: an explicit reconstructed, non-model-based witness (optimistic Hedge with backward induction and adaptive generative queries), with a universal constant C (the proof gives C = 20000). Whether Q-FTRL attains the rates is not checked; the printed theorem is therefore shown as incomplete, with this existence result as a related proved result (project decision 2026-11-10; C39).
